Legs.Subject: Profiled counts match independent small and published counts at 0, 1000, 10^10 and 2^40, plus the independent 64-integer window above 2^40.
Legs.Against: Exact small counts and Oliveira e Silva's Tables IV/V; Oracles.ExactPrimality supplies the checkpoint delta without production counting or sieve code.
Legs.Citation: https://sweet.ua.pt/tos/bib/5.4.pdf, Tables IV/V. ENVELOPE: cheap routes only; no Gourdon work count is inferred from result agreement.

Legs.Subject: Adding request-local profiling preserves the production result at the count fixtures.
Legs.Against: The ordinary PrimeCountingFunction result for the same input.
Legs.Shared: Both call the identical CountPrimeBound64 dispatcher and selected counting kernels; this equality establishes diagnostic transparency only.
Legs.Citation: The separate classical leg supplies the independent numeric expectations.

Legs.Subject: CountOnly has one bound/route record and no selection work; non-Gourdon routes leave all Gourdon fields zero. The checkpoint delta [2^40+1,2^40+64] marks one logical 3-byte bitmap because 2^40 has remainder 16 modulo 30, narrow enough to presieve without a windowed upper-base pass.
Legs.Citation: ENVELOPE: zero isolation checks read every Gourdon field but do not establish correctness of nonzero Gourdon counters. Counter units exclude allocations, uint-kernel internals, base generation and individual sieve marks.

Legs.Subject: Profiled nth-prime selection agrees at a narrow index, an out-of-range index, ranks 32 below/above 2^40 and the last ulong rank.
Legs.Against: Small prime31, zero for a rank beyond the finite prime count, and Oracles.ExactPrimality over independent local windows; published pi(2^40) and pi(2^64) fix the indices.
Legs.Citation: https://sweet.ua.pt/tos/bib/5.4.pdf, Table V. ENVELOPE: checkpoint and narrow selections only, not distant count-guided inversion.

Legs.Subject: Profiling preserves ordinary NthPrime results at the same selected inputs.
Legs.Shared: Both call identical NthPrime64 selection and counting paths.
Legs.Citation: The separate classical leg fixes the expected prime independently.

Legs.Subject: Narrow/out-of-range routes have no counted work. Both 32-rank checkpoint directions request exactly one selection window and one marked segment with no count dispatch. Selecting the final prime makes 30 odd-candidate primality requests and no bitmap request.
Legs.Citation: ENVELOPE: these are exact request-level work counts for fixed routes, not instruction counts or timings. The cases do not force window exhaustion or inspect per-mark work.

Legs.Subject: A second profiled request leaves the first result and frozen count record unchanged. A mutable-list interface, if exposed, rejects replacement. Pre-canceled count and nth requests throw OperationCanceledException before route selection.
Legs.Citation: ENVELOPE: sequential request isolation and public collection immutability; this does not inject cancellation during an expensive count or prove simultaneous-call scheduling.
